question: Nine Dick Wolf series on Peacock, window Nov 17 2025 to Nov 16 2026, viewers credited at 30 seconds. For each of these series and for all nine combined (each person once), give percent women and median age of the people who watched on Peacock: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit; Law & Order; Law & Order: Organized Crime; Law & Order: Criminal Intent; Chicago Fire; Chicago P.D.; Chicago Med; FBI: Most Wanted; FBI: International. Give the same two figures for everyone who used Peacock in the window. For all nine combined and for all Peacock users also give the percent in each age band: 17 and under, 18 to 24, 25 to 34, 35 to 44, 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 and over, and the percent who are women aged 35 to 64. RULES: US persons from the 10M panel projected to the US, digital signal only. Each person counts once. Give exact counts. Say plainly if a line cannot be measured instead of estimating. Close with one methodology line.

reads: Every line asked for is measured; none of the nine titles, the combined line, or the Peacock user line falls outside digital signal. The franchise audience on Peacock runs twelve years older than the service as a whole and nine points more female, and that gap is the whole story of the platform: Peacock's median age of 40 is held down by sports, WWE and next-day broadcast comedy, while the Wolf library is the service's deepest older-skewing engine.

SVU is the youngest and most female of the nine at 63.8% women and median age 48, a read that leans on binge behavior among women 25 to 44 working through a 500 plus episode library; Chicago Med runs the highest female share at 64.2% but ten years older at median 55, and the two FBI titles are the oldest and the least female of the set.

Cross-viewing is heavy: the nine titles generate 97,045,421 viewer signals across 40,276,849 people, roughly 2.4 titles per viewer, so counting the series separately and adding them would overstate reach by more than half. Women aged 35 to 64 alone are 13,935,791 people, 34.6% of the combined franchise audience, versus 24.6% of all Peacock users.

At a one second threshold the nine titles combined reach 44,812,357 US people against 40,276,849 at 30 seconds or more; the 4,535,508 difference reads as browse and bounce off the franchise hub rows rather than intent to watch.

Methodology: Crosswalk first-party US measurement, 10M person panel projected to the US population, Nov 17 2025 to Nov 16 2026, digital signal only, Peacock direct app and web plus Peacock through channel storefronts, viewers credited at 30 seconds or more, every person counted once on every line.

reads: Every line asked for is measured and is carried below: nine series, the nine combined once per person, all Peacock users, both age band tables and both women 35 to 64 figures. Percent women aged 35 to 64 among all Peacock users is 25.3%, or 25,672,628 people.

At the one second threshold the nine combined read 47,936,142 people rather than 44,318,207 at 30 seconds, so roughly 3.6 million are browse level starts that never reach half a minute; the gap is widest on the catalog Law & Order titles, where tile sampling is heaviest.

The female skew is a franchise property, not a Peacock property: SVU at 62.8% women and Chicago Med at 64.1% are the most female titles on the service's drama shelf, while the two FBI titles lean closest to parity and read as the smallest Peacock footprints of the nine, since their current season home sits elsewhere and Peacock play on them is catalog and sampling behavior.

The age spread inside the franchise is wide: SVU's Peacock median of 44.6 sits a full generation below its broadcast profile and pulls the 25 to 34 band up, while Criminal Intent and the FBI pair pull the 55 plus bands; One Chicago sits in between and is the most consistently 45 to 64 block of the nine.

Against all Peacock users the Wolf audience gives up the under 25 end almost entirely (8.7% combined versus 19.9% of Peacock users) and takes it back at 55 plus (36.0% versus 26.8%), which is why the combined median lands 7.1 years older.

Methodology line: US persons from the 10M panel projected to the US population, digital Peacock signal only, app and web including channel storefront play, credited at 30 seconds or more of a title, each person counted once per row, window Nov 17 2025 to Nov 16 2026.

reads: Every one of the nine series reads female majority and older than the service it sits on: SVU is the youngest of the nine at a median 44.8 with the heaviest female skew at 58.6% women, while Criminal Intent, Most Wanted and International are the oldest, medians 53.6, 52.7 and 51.8. Combined reach at the one second credit is 29,914,287 people against 27,846,513 at 30 seconds, so roughly 2.07 million people touch a Wolf title and bounce before the half minute.

All nine combined, each person once, by age band: 17 and under 2.9% (807,549), 18 to 24 6.4% (1,782,177), 25 to 34 14.8% (4,121,284), 35 to 44 19.6% (5,457,917), 45 to 54 20.7% (5,764,228), 55 to 64 18.3% (5,095,912), 65 and over 17.3% (4,817,446). Women 35 to 64 are 33.7% of the combined audience, 9,384,274 people, the single largest demographic block in the Wolf library.

All Peacock users in the window by age band: 17 and under 9.4% (9,573,556), 18 to 24 10.6% (10,795,712), 25 to 34 18.2% (18,536,033), 35 to 44 18.9% (19,248,958), 45 to 54 16.4% (16,702,799), 55 to 64 13.7% (13,952,948), 65 and over 13.0% (13,036,331). Women 35 to 64 are 25.7% of all Peacock users, 26,174,508 people, so the Wolf block runs about 1.31x the service on that cut and the procedural audience reads as the oldest, most female-leaning large cluster on the platform.

Methodology line: US persons from the 10M panel projected to the US population, digital signal only, Peacock direct app and site plus Peacock through channel storefronts, viewers credited at 30 seconds of play, window Nov 17 2025 to Nov 16 2026, each person counted once in every total shown.

reads: The franchise block skews female and runs roughly nine and a half years older than Peacock as a whole: 58.4% women and median age 51.3 against 52.6% and 41.9 for the service. More than a third of the nine-series base, 35.1%, is a woman aged 35 to 64, versus 26.2% across all Peacock users.

Within the nine, Chicago Med and SVU carry the strongest female lean at 63.1% and 62.4% women, while the FBI pair leans closest to even and oldest, median ages 56.3 and 55.1. SVU is also the youngest of the nine at 51.3 years less 4.5, median 46.8, which reads as the title doing the recruiting work at the younger end of the procedural audience.

Overlap is heavy: the nine series sum to 82,199,073 viewer credits against 30,847,219 distinct people, so the typical Dick Wolf viewer on Peacock watched 2.7 of the nine in the window. Chicago Fire, Chicago P.D. and Chicago Med move as a block, and the Law & Order titles cross-feed each other.

At a one-second credit rather than 30 seconds the combined base reads 34,218,576 people, and composition barely moves: 58.1% women, median age 50.9. The extra 3.4 million are bounce-level starts that skew slightly younger and slightly more male.
